note: phases is the executable plan run-workflow.sh follows (a test asserts they agree); pipeline is the same plan as prose with {claude} and {codex} standing for whichever model the tier or the seats override puts in that seat; seats pins a model for a condition regardless of tier, which is how the mixed-tier arms are defined.

conditions.label: fable-solo
conditions.description: Fable investigates, edits, and tests once.

conditions.label: cross-vendor-bounce
conditions.description: Fable implements; Codex reviews and repairs the patch.

conditions.label: fable-led-panel
conditions.description: Fable implements; Codex, GLM, and Kimi critique; Fable repairs.

conditions.label: fable-self-bounce
conditions.description: Fable implements and performs a second review/repair pass.

conditions.label: codex-solo
conditions.description: Codex investigates, edits, and tests once.

conditions.label: glm-solo-single-shot
conditions.description: GLM receives the issue plus retrieved file context and returns one unified diff. No agent loop, no test execution.
conditions.pipeline: glm answers once, from retrieved context

conditions.label: kimi-solo-single-shot
conditions.description: Kimi receives the issue plus retrieved file context and returns one unified diff. No agent loop, no test execution.
conditions.pipeline: kimi answers once, from retrieved context

conditions.label: fable-glm-bounce
conditions.description: Fable implements; GLM returns one single-shot critique with no agent loop; Fable repairs.

conditions.label: fable-kimi-bounce
conditions.description: Fable implements; Kimi returns one single-shot critique with no agent loop; Fable repairs.

conditions.label: codex-implements-fable-repairs
conditions.description: The reverse of B: Codex implements; Fable reviews and repairs. Tests whether a reviewer stronger than the author explains B's gain (the KDD'26 asymmetry).

conditions.label: codex-self-bounce
conditions.description: Codex implements, then reviews and repairs its own patch. The self-bounce control for the Codex seat, as D is for the Claude seat.

conditions.label: fable-best-of-2
conditions.description: Two independent Fable implementations; the repository's own tests pick one, with no reviewer. The equal-cost baseline for D: two dispatches either way.
conditions.pipeline: {claude} implements twice → repo tests pick one

conditions.label: sonnet-to-sol-bounce
conditions.description: Mixed tier: Sonnet implements; gpt-5.6-sol reviews and repairs. The product question: does a cheap implementer with a strong reviewer match a strong solo at lower cost?

conditions.label: fable-to-terra-bounce
conditions.description: Mixed tier: Fable implements; gpt-5.6-terra reviews and repairs. The cheap-reviewer half of the tier crossing.

conditions.label: sol-implements-fable-repairs
conditions.description: The reverse of frontier B: gpt-5.6-sol implements; Fable reviews and repairs.

conditions.label: cross-vendor-bounce-2-rounds
conditions.description: B with a second review/repair round: Fable implements; Codex repairs; Codex reviews the repaired patch and repairs again.
